title: Samlion
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Sotah 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.13b.24), Samlion says, “Moses, the great scribe of Israel, died there.” Hyman also cites Sifrei, Berakhah 34. Rashi explains Samlion as a sage's name; the Arukh, under Samlion, explains it as an angel's name.[^1][^2]

notes.text: [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sotah.13b.24.2) reads Samlion as a sage. [Tosafot](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Sotah.13b.24.1) record both sage and angel interpretations, as does [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2816&lang=en). Hyman attributes the angel reading to the Arukh.

The Hebrew of [Sifrei Devarim 357](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Devarim.357.28) reads “Samlion said” beside “Moses died there,” without the phrase “the great scribe of Israel” found in Sotah. The consulted English translation follows the alternative interpretation “this is suggested,” while its note records the personal-name reading. Hyman’s Berakhah 34 is his printed locator.
